text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where the tape looked like this, SPY and its analogs produced a median 5-session return of -0.1%, with outcomes ranging from -5.12% to 6.88%. The single number to anchor on is that median max adverse excursion of -1.05%, which describes how far underwater the path typically went before the week was over.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs because the current state is defined by unusually thin liquidity and a sharp oil move: the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) sits at -1.985, WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is 19.24%, and 20-session realised volatility (vol20) is compressed at 9.16%. The reference close is 761.69 as of 2026-09-18. Macro context shows a VIX level of 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a Fed funds target change over 90 days of 0.25 bp. Equity market sentiment registers at 57.1 in the "Greed" band, though the CNN Business Fear & Greed cross-check reads 38.3 in "fear", driven by extreme fear readings in stock price strength and breadth. Headlines framing this market right now include Yahoo Finance reporting "Nasdaq, S&P 500, Dow Futures Steady Ahead Of Fed Minutes This Week" and CNBC noting "Treasury yields hold near multiyear highs as traders await data, Fed minutes this week." Crypto sentiment reads 70 ("Greed") on alternative.me, but that is the mood of the crypto market only, relevant solely as context for the tokenised wrapper discussed later.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs spanning 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-08, the mean 5-session return was -0.03% and the median was -0.1%, with a standard deviation of 2.14%. The distribution leans slightly positive with a skew of 0.51, but the left tail is populated: 52% of episodes finished below zero, while the 10th percentile was -2.39% and the worst outcome was -5.12%. The closest match was IWM on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2997), which fell -2.98% over five sessions. SPY itself appeared seven times in the set; the SPY session on 2026-09-03 (distance 0.3101) returned -1.15%, while the SPY session on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.3366) rallied 3.47%. JPM on 2026-09-04 (distance 0.3418) dropped -2.37%. The bad tail is dominated by recent broad ETF weakness, particularly those September 2026 sessions.

[tails]
A position can finish near flat and still be un-holdable mid-week. In these 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -1.05%, meaning the typical path dipped more than 1% below the entry price at some point during the five sessions. The 25th percentile of adverse excursion was -1.98%, and the 10th percentile was -3.1%. Conversely, the median max favourable excursion was 0.99%. Looking at drawdown breaches, 4% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown threshold intra-horizon, while 0% breached 10%, 15%, or 20%. The reward-to-risk ratio based on excursions was 0.94.

[stress]
The baseline median across all 50 analogs is -0.1%. Under the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario, the median forward return worsened to -4.61% (a delta of -4.51%), with 48 analogs used; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, making it a sample of one regime rather than a forecast. The 2025-04 tariff shock scenario produced a median of -0.92% (delta -0.82%) using 26 analogs; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation / rate bear scenario yielded a median of -2.09% (delta -1.99%) on 50 analogs; caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare gave a median of -1.09% (delta -0.99%) on 50 analogs; caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters late-window analogs. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind showed a median of -0.49% (delta -0.39%) on 36 analogs; caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2023-03 regional bank stress actually improved the median to 1.41% (delta 1.51%) on 36 analogs; caveat: very short window dominated by a handful of sessions. A +2 sigma VIX spike gave -0.2% (delta -0.1%) on 50 analogs; caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. Earnings release day produced -0.79% (delta -0.69%) on 50 analogs; caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. Liquidity air pocket gave -0.13% (delta -0.03%) on 50 analogs; caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, bounding reference-market gap risk only, while the measured tokenised wrapper (SPY/USDT on Bitget) saw 61.18% of its hourly movement in closed hours. FOMC decision day gave -0.11% (delta -0.01%) on 50 analogs; caveat: only 92 decision days exist, so the set is small and highly overlapping. Policy-rate path re-pricing gave 0.07% (delta 0.17%) on 50 analogs; caveat: uses DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies, and transmission depends on duration not captured here. Crypto drawdown contagion gave 0.77% (delta 0.87%) on 50 analogs; caveat: BTC feature is a market-wide proxy, and fng is excluded from the distance metric. China ADR de-rating gave 0.16% (delta 0.26%) on 50 analogs; caveat: delisting risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space. Weekend hold on the 7x24 venue gave -0.21% (delta -0.11%) on 50 analogs; caveat: blocks are paired by index modulo block count, a deterministic convention, and the measured window holds only a handful of distinct weekends. No scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three most relevant scenarios for this idea are the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash, because the current dv20z of -1.985 directly mirrors a liquidity void and that scenario pushed the median to -4.61% with a 41.7% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; the 2022 inflation / rate bear, because the 19.24% oilChg20 aligns with an inflationary regime that dragged the median to -2.09% across 50 analogs; and the 2025-04 tariff shock, because it represents a discrete policy shock that worsened the median by -0.82% to -0.92% despite using only 26 analogs. A concentration to distrust is the heavy weighting of 2025 (26 analogs) and 2026 (14 analogs) in the retrieval set, meaning the distribution is overwhelmingly shaped by the last two years rather than a broad historical base. The 2023-03 regional bank stress scenario contradicts the generally negative baseline direction, producing a positive median of 1.41%, showing that idiosyncratic sector rotation does not always drag the broad index down.

[limits]
The engine's own honest verdict states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The directional hit rate is 50.1%. Out-of-sample conformal coverage was 80.8% against an 80% target, but the matched coverage width was 10.2% versus 9.48% for the unconditional name benchmark, confirming the lack of sharpness. For path risk validation at the 10% drawdown level, the realised breach rate out of sample was 2%, while the mean predicted rate from the analog excursion share was 3.4%, yielding a calibration gap of 1.4 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 0.48 pp. The analog Brier score MAE was 0.0196, beating the vol reflection benchmark (0.0241), the same-name calibration (0.024), and the pooled calibration (0.021). The paired Brier confidence intervals resolve all three comparisons, as none span zero: the interval versus vol reflection is [-0.0071, -0.0022], versus same-name is [-0.0059, -0.0029], and versus pooled is [-0.0023, -0.0005]. The wrapper status is "measured". On the primary venue (Bitget official MCP, SPY/USDT perpetual), the reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 61.18% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is a "fair tracker" with a return correlation of 0.9477 and a tracking error of 23 bp/day. The basis band is -0.04% to 0.31%, and the spread is 0.13 bps. Caveat: a fair perpetual is not the underlying and carries funding and idiosyncratic risk; nothing here feeds the retrieval engine. Across 6 observed weekend blocks, the median weekend return was -0.101%, the 10th percentile was -0.506%, the standard deviation was 0.4191%, and the median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.2125%; 0% of those weekends breached a 5% drawdown. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions of the underlying.
